synthetic_controls.claim: Intervention A reduces the incidence of condition R in initially unaffected adults compared with placebo.
sources: A randomized placebo-controlled trial in adults initially free of condition R found that intervention A reduced new diagnoses of condition R from 20% to 10% over five years, with a statistically significant difference.

A large adequately powered randomized placebo-controlled trial in adults initially free of condition R found identical five-year incidence of new condition R diagnoses with intervention A and placebo. The trial excluded a clinically meaningful reduction in incidence.
A randomized trial in adults already diagnosed with condition R found intervention A did not slow symptom progression compared with placebo. The trial did not measure prevention of onset.

An observational survey found lower incidence of condition R among adults who chose intervention A. There was no randomized assignment or placebo comparator, and confounding precludes a causal conclusion.
